title: O Happy They Who Know the Lord
description: O Happy They Who Know the Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 46, “Gospel privileges”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O hap-py they who know the Lord, With whom he deigns to dwell! He feeds and cheers them by his word, His arm sup-ports them well.

lines: O happy they who know the Lord,
With whom he deigns to dwell!
He feeds and cheers them by his word,
His arm supports them well.
To them, in each distressing hour,
His throne of grace is near;
And when they plead his love and pow'r,
He stands engaged to hear.
He helped his saints in ancient days
Who trusted in his name;
And we can witness, to his praise,
His love is still the same.
Wand'ring in sin, our souls he found,
And bid us seek his face;
Gave us to hear the gospel sound,
And taste the gospel grace.
Oft in his house his glory shines
Before our wond'ring eyes;
We wish not, then, for golden mines,
Or ought beneath the skies.
His presence sweetens all our cares,
And makes our burdens light;
A word from him dispels our fears,
And gilds the gloom of night.
Lord, we expect to suffer here,
Nor would we dare repine;
But give us, still, to find thee near;
And own us, still, for thine.
Let us enjoy, and highly prize
These tokens of thy love;
Till thou shalt bid our spirits rise,
To worship thee above.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
